recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if a work group wants new, broader Provenance-versus-extension policy text across all resources; FHIR-3118 itself is adequately reflected in current Provenance and Composition source.
issue_request: FHIR-3118 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for FHIR-core Composition, applied for DSTU1. It asked why Composition.author, Composition.attester, and Composition.custodian were not represented only as Provenance resources, and the accepted resolution was to add guidance explaining overlap with resource-specific elements, when Provenance is appropriate for additional participation information, when an extension or resource element is better, and when both can coexist.
initial_application: The Jira comments identify SVN revision 3272 as the first application. In git, commit 062b3297ff2b4a5f67a429140d477bb370bca4fc added a Relationship with other resources section to source/provenance/provenance-introduction.xml stating that other resources may overlap with Provenance, that those resource elements should be preferred, and that Provenance is for additional information or overlapping provenance records.
additional_context: Provenance and Composition are active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini. The current Provenance introduction preserves and strengthens the FHIR-3118 guidance in the Boundaries and Relationships section, adds a FiveWs overlap link, and the Provenance StructureDefinition root comment explicitly says parties may be duplicated between a target resource and its provenance. Current Composition also directly models author, attester, custodian, and, after later Applied issue FHIR-50984, participant for other clinical-document participants; the participant binding text excludes author/authenticator/custodian because those are already distinct named fields. Exact Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-3118 and the relevant Provenance/Composition terms found no contrary community record.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already tells implementers to use resource-specific elements in preference to Provenance while allowing Provenance when explicit provenance/record information is needed, and Composition now provides a first-class participant element for the additional-contributor use case that motivated the original question.

related_jiras.note: Added Composition.participant for other clinical-document participants, directly covering the additional-contributor scenario that prompted FHIR-3118 without changing the Provenance overlap rule.
